note: Window agent p1670-p1679. Entries: Sweden/Denmark-Norway speckle, Fezzan occupation, Qing keyframe spans and rebel zone, Acadia, New Mexico.

region.text: present Sweden (2,440 cells); a gain moves only the cells Denmark-Norway holds there: the Jamtland, Harjedalen and Idre-Sarna border cells ceded at Bromsebro (1645) and any other Danish-Norwegian speckle

events.note: Jan 1670: about 50 cells of present Sweden (Dalarna 13, Vastra Gotaland 11, Vasterbotten 10, Kronoberg 7 and others) sit in the Denmark-Norway shape, which the size rule keeps against Sweden. The page: 'with the Treaty of Brömsebro in 1645, Denmark–Norway had to cede some of their territories' including 'Norwegian territories Jemtland, Herjedalen and Idre & Serna'; its undated account of Roskilde (1658) gives Sweden Bohuslan and the Danish mainland provinces, and the Copenhagen sentence of 1660 returns only 'Trondelag and Bornholm'. Together with the denmark-norway_1670 override this hands the cells to Sweden. Reviewer: the earlier spec 'Sweden minus Norway and Denmark' resolved to the same 2,440 cells, so it is written as present Sweden; with the other windows' patches applied the trial moves 3 cells (two in Jamtland, one at Idre).

Reverses ledger/3, which hands the Fezzan to the Ottoman empire outright in 1679 and leaves the dynasty with no land until 1682. The page says only 'It was occupied fully from times to time like in 1679-1682, 1690, 1716, 1718 and 1811/1812'; the Awlad Muhammad page has an Ottoman army kill the sultan in 1682 and his son al-Nasir 'agreed to pay tribute', so the dynasty carried on. An occupation, not an annexation (next entry).

1679: the Fezzan is 'occupied fully from times to time like in 1679-1682'; the Ottoman side is the dossier's reading (Tripoli's regency; the Awlad Muhammad page names 'an ottoman army led by Murad al-Malti' in 1682). Drawn as an occupation of the dynasty's land.
1682: the span '1679-1682' ends (ledger/4 takes the same year for the recovery). Closes the occupation opened in 1679; outside the window 1670-1679 (the next window sees it open on 1 January 1680).

correction.text: the Qing without Yunnan and Guizhou, where Wu Sangui revolted in December 1673

keyframe_overrides.why: The keyframe takes its years from Cliopatria's shape, 1673-1676, so in 1674-1676 the union of the Qing keyframes alive includes this wider shape and swallows qing-dynasty_1674 and _1676. At the 1674 snap the Qing take back 2,757 cells (Sichuan, Guangxi, Hunan) that the ledger gave to the rebels, and Wu Sangui holds them only from 1676 (keyframe snap, 2,841 cells). The page: 'In 1680, the provinces of Hunan, Guizhou, Guangxi, and Sichuan were recovered by the Qing', so they were rebel land before; the wu-sangui-s-zhou dossier has them from April 1674. Explicit years 1673-1673 make the 1674 and 1676 keyframes act.

union.text: Sichuan as the Qing province stood: Sichuan with the Chongqing area

correction.text: Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Guangxi, Sichuan and Guangdong: Fujian is no longer Wu's at the end of 1676 (Geng's surrender)

keyframe_overrides.why: The 1676 shape (1676-1676) keeps Fujian 'before Geng's surrender', which cancels the dossier's own ledger/5 (Fujian to the Qing in 1676, 'Geng Jingzhong surrendered in 1676') at the year-end snap; at 1677 the Wu keyframe, which has no Fujian, then drops the 490 cells to nobody and they stay nobody's until the 1678 Qing keyframe. The page: 'As a result, after 1676, the tide turned in favor of the Qing forces.' The Qing 1676 shape is changed to match (next entry). Reviewer: the year is on the Geng Jingzhong page ('in 1674 Geng Jingzhong rebelled against Qing rule'; he 'surrendered in 1676 and pledged his support to putting down the other revolting feudatories'), so the source is that page; Shang Zhixin's Guangdong in 1676 stays on the Revolt page ('In 1676, Shang Zhixin joined the rebellion, consolidating Guangdong under his rule').

union.text: Zheng Jing's Fujian coast, held by Tungning 1674 to March/April 1677 (as kingdom-of-tungning_1674)

correction.text: the Qing without the six rebel provinces of 1676 (Fujian is Qing again after Geng's surrender) and without Zheng Jing's Fujian coast (Xiamen, Quanzhou, Zhangzhou)

keyframe_overrides.why: Companion of the wu-sangui-s-zhou_1676 override: Fujian goes back to the Qing in 1676 (ledger/5 of the Wu dossier) instead of staying with the rebels to the end of the year. The page: 'after 1676, the tide turned in favor of the Qing forces.' Reviewer: Geng Jingzhong page: he 'surrendered in 1676'. Tungning's Xiamen, Quanzhou and Zhangzhou are cut out as well: with Fujian in the Qing shape the succession rule (R2) gave 56 of Tungning's coastal cells to the Qing in 1676, though the Kingdom of Tungning page has Zheng Jing take 'Quanzhou and Zhangzhou in 1674' and lose Quanzhou only 'on 12 March 1677' and Zhangzhou 'on 5 April'.

minus.text: Tungning's mainland holds 1677-1679, Xiamen, Haicheng and Chaozhou (as kingdom-of-tungning_1677), held until the mainland war ended in April 1680

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1677 Qing shape plus the rest of the rebel zone (its Southern Ming row) outside Wu's core: Fujian, Guangdong, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Shaanxi and Gansu are Qing; Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Sichuan, Chongqing and Guangxi stay Wu's, Taiwan Tungning's; without Tungning's mainland holds (Xiamen, Haicheng, Chaozhou) until 1680

keyframe_overrides.why: The 'ok' 1677 shape is Cliopatria's Qing without the whole rebel zone (Southern Ming row, 1.93 M km2, the land the Qing hold again by 1683), so at 1677 the snap strips 1,791 cells of Fujian (467), Guangdong (693), Hubei (230), Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Shaanxi and Gansu from the Qing and they stay nobody's through 1679, though the ledger had already returned them. The page: 'after 1676, the tide turned in favor of the Qing forces', Wang Fuchen 'surrendered after a three-year-long stalemate' (rising 1674), and only 'Hunan, Guizhou, Guangxi, and Sichuan' (plus Yunnan) were still to be recovered in 1680-1681; Shang Zhixin page: after Shang Kexi's death in late 1676 he 'changed his mind and defected back to the Qing'. Same construction as p1680-p1689 qing-dynasty_1680. Reviewer: Tungning's Xiamen, Haicheng and Chaozhou (kingdom-of-tungning_1677) are cut out: with Fujian and Guangdong in the Qing shape the succession rule (R2) gave those 34 cells to the Qing at the 1677/1678 snaps, though the Revolt page has 'Zheng Jing's forces were defeated near Xiamen in 1680 and forced to withdraw to Taiwan' and the Kingdom of Tungning page has Haicheng retaken 'in August' 1677 and the mainland war closing 'On 10 April' 1680. qing-dynasty_1677 keeps its Cliopatria span 1677-1682, so this shape joins the union at the 1680 and 1682 snaps (both wider, no effect).

The page: 'In 1678, Wu finally proclaimed himself emperor of the Great Zhou Dynasty'; 'In 1680, the provinces of Hunan, Guizhou, Guangxi, and Sichuan were recovered by the Qing'. Reviewer: Tungning's Xiamen, Haicheng and Chaozhou (kingdom-of-tungning_1677) are cut out: with Fujian and Guangdong in the Qing shape the succession rule (R2) gave those 34 cells to the Qing at the 1677/1678 snaps, though the Revolt page has 'Zheng Jing's forces were defeated near Xiamen in 1680 and forced to withdraw to Taiwan' and the Kingdom of Tungning page has Haicheng retaken 'in August' 1677 and the mainland war closing 'On 10 April' 1680. qing-dynasty_1677 keeps its Cliopatria span 1677-1682, so this shape joins the union at the 1680 and 1682 snaps (both wider, no effect).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1670 Denmark-Norway shape without the cells it draws inside present Sweden

keyframe_overrides.why: The shape (1670-1708) draws about 50 cells in Sweden, which the size rule keeps for Denmark-Norway (60 cell-years of conflict in 1670; Dalarna 13, Vastra Gotaland 11, Vasterbotten 10, Kronoberg 7, ...). The page: 'with the Treaty of Brömsebro in 1645, Denmark–Norway had to cede ... Norwegian territories Jemtland, Herjedalen and Idre & Serna'; the 1660 sentence returns only 'Trondelag and Bornholm' to Denmark-Norway, so Bohuslan and the rest of the ceded provinces stay Swedish. The span reaches 1708, beyond this window.

union.text: The North American cells of Cliopatria's 1670 shape only, without Saint-Domingue (82 cells, Haiti), Cayenne (67 cells, French Guiana), Reunion (9 cells), the Antilles and Madagascar. New France 'consisted of five colonies at its peak in 1712' and 'extended from Newfoundland to the Canadian Prairies and from Hudson Bay to the Gulf of Mexico' (Canada, Acadia, Hudson Bay, Terre-Neuve, Louisiana); Cliopatria's row also holds other French colonies.
Acadia, the Port-Royal region and the Bay of Fundy shore

correction.text: the North American cells of Cliopatria's 1670 shape plus Acadia (Nova Scotia and New Brunswick cells of the 1673 shape), back with France from 1670

keyframe_overrides.why: new-france ledger/13 gives Acadia back to France in 1670, but the 1670 keyframe (1670-1672) is Cliopatria's shape without it, so the snap takes the 53 Nova Scotia and New Brunswick cells away again until the 1673 keyframe returns them. The page: England held Acadia 'again from 1654 until 1670', and its capital was at Castine (1670-1674), so France holds it through 1670-1672.

Buayan's core round Sarangani Bay (the Spanish 'could not occupy Buayan itself'; vassal only from 10 March 1887)

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1677 Spanish Empire shape with New Mexico (kept until the Pueblo Revolt of August 1680; ledger/34 removes it in 1680), without the Cotabato Valley (Maguindanao) and Buayan's Sarangani Bay core

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's 1677 correction (years 1677-1682) cuts New Mexico out for the whole span, so the snap at 1677 empties 67 cells three years before the Pueblo Revolt, although its own ledger/34 loses them in 1680. The page: the Puebloans rose on 'August 10' 1680; 'on August 21, New Mexico Governor Antonio de Otermín' led the Spaniards out of Santa Fe; the 1670s bring drought and unrest ('came to a head in 1675'), not a Spanish withdrawal. Shape years cut to 1677-1679; ledger/34 (1680) removes New Mexico. Reviewer: in the current compile New Mexico is held by viceroyalty-of-new-spain (p1600-p1609 events/0), and the Spanish 1677 snap no longer fires, so this entry moves no cell at present; it keeps the keyframe consistent with the page.
